I have all the data I need. Here is the complete analysis.

## Data source and method
Counts come from the **`cancer_prognostic_data`** HPA bulk file. A gene is counted as a **validated favourable** (or **unfavourable**) prognostic gene for a TCGA cohort when the corresponding `validated prognostic - favorable` / `validated prognostic - unfavorable` column contains a p-value (non-empty). Each gene appears once per cancer (verified: counts equal distinct-gene counts), and no gene is simultaneously favourable and unfavourable in the same cancer, so **total = favourable + unfavourable**. There are **21 TCGA cohorts** in the HPA cancer prognostics data.

Note: 11 of the 21 TCGA cohorts have **no** validated prognostic genes (all-zero rows), so the grouped bar chart shows bars only for the 10 cohorts with non-zero counts (unless you keep the 11 zero-cohorts on the axis).

## Ten cancers with the most prognostic genes in total (dot plot data)
Sorted descending by total: **KIRC 1903, LIHC 1052, LUAD 207, PAAD 138, GBM 69, OV 17, READ 11, BRCA 9, COAD 8, LUSC 5**. These are exactly the 10 cohorts with ≥1 validated prognostic gene.

Key takeaways from the data:
- **KIRC** dominates with 1903 validated prognostic genes (1639 favourable, 264 unfavourable) — the most of any TCGA cohort.
- **LIHC** is second (1052) and is heavily **unfavourable-weighted** (939 unfavourable vs 113 favourable).
- LUAD (207), PAAD (138) and GBM (69) follow, all unfavourable-dominated; OV, READ, BRCA, COAD and LUSC round out the ten with far smaller numbers.
- Because KIRC dwarfs the rest, on a linear axis the grouped bar chart will visually flatten all other cohorts; a log scale or a chart restricted to the 10 non-zero cohorts is more readable if needed.
